chunk_findings.detail: The replacement does not show that a past-deadline scratch merge kills git or drops the worker. It stubs `W.git` so that any call whose args start with `-c` and contain `merge` returns `timed_out` immediately, then asserts `UNAVAILABLE`. A `merge` invocation that does not start with `-c` (for example `git(wt, "merge", ..., timeout=remaining)`) skips the stub, runs the real merge of `ddflow/clean` into `main`, and returns `CLEAN`, so the assertion fails even when the deadline was forwarded. Conversely, an implementation that only forwards `timeout=` and still leaves the child and worktree running — the bug `test_known_limit_the_scratch_worker_outlives_the_deadline` existed to catch, and which this diff deletes — still passes, because the stub never starts a process that can outlive `timeout_s=1`.

chunk_findings.detail: `deadline_s` is applied as a fresh per-call `timeout` on worktree add, rev-parse, merge-base, and merge, not as one budget for the whole scratch merge. Given `probe_timeout_s=5`, a slow `worktree add` can run 5s and then `merge` another 5s (and merge-base yet another 5s if it is killed: non-zero `.code` is treated as "not an ancestor" and the merge is still attempted). `probe._scratch` now blocks in-process on `CI.merge_tree` with no outer cap, so the CLI stays alive well past `[locks].probe_timeout_s` — the outliving-the-deadline failure this change claims to close.

chunk_findings.detail: `left()` is `cutoff - time.monotonic()` with no floor, while `W.scratch_tree` is still given the original `deadline_s` as its own timer, which starts after `cutoff`. A worktree add that finishes inside that timer but after the shared cutoff makes `left()` negative, and the next call is `W.git(..., timeout=left())`. `subprocess` rejects a negative timeout with `ValueError` instead of a cannot-merge/`timed_out` result. Given `deadline_s=5`, add starts ~50ms after `cutoff` with `timeout=5` and returns at cutoff+10ms: `rev-parse`/`merge-base` is invoked with `timeout≈-0.01` and the probe raises rather than reporting unavailable.

chunk_findings.detail: The replacement never runs a merge past a deadline and never checks that a git child is killed or that the process does not outlive the probe. chunk_findings.detail:
`resolve_patch` reads `--diff`/`--blob` with `Path.read_text("utf-8")`, which enables universal newlines and only accepts UTF-8. A patch whose bytes are `diff --git a/f b/f
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+hello
` is returned as `+hello
`, so the suggestion drops the CR and changes the wrong content. The same call raises uncaught `UnicodeDecodeError` (not `SuggestError`) when a hunk contains a non-UTF-8 byte such as `0xFF`. `UnicodeDecodeError` is not an `OSError`, and the commit path’s `--binary` form is not subject to this check.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/handoff/send.py:60

chunk_findings.detail: `_owner_tip` treats every non-ok `rev-parse` as “no branch” and returns `item.base`. `git.run` results expose `unavailable` (used in `resolve_patch`), but this path ignores it. If `rev-parse` of `refs/heads/ddflow/{item}` is unavailable, a real owner tip is replaced with a stale `base` (or `""`) and `suggest` still proposes, so the change is re-cut onto the wrong commit instead of failing closed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/handoff.py:24

chunk_findings.detail: `--commit` is turned into a patch with `git show --format= --binary <commit>`, which for a merge prints a combined diff and is often empty even when the merge has parent changes. Given merge `M` whose first parent lacks files that `M` contains, `resolve_patch` returns `""` (or a combined diff that is not `M^1..M`) and that wrong patch is what `propose` records. The stated contract is the change versus the parent (`git diff M^1 M` / `git show -m`), which this command does not produce.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/handoff/send.py:52

chunk_findings.detail: The declared `suggest` command has no `--evidence` param and `_suggest` never forwards one, so `ddflow suggest ITEM --diff F --reason R --kind gate_fix --evidence pytest,0` cannot record CMD,EXIT. The tool schema only accepts item, reason, commit, diff, blob, and kind; the flag is rejected or dropped, and a gate_fix suggestion is stored with no probe evidence.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/handoff.py:41

chunk_findings.detail: `Path.read_text("utf-8")` only traps `OSError`. `UnicodeDecodeError` is a `ValueError`, so it is not turned into `SuggestError`. `api.handoff.suggest` only catches `SuggestError`. A `--diff` or `--blob` file whose body is a real git patch of a non-UTF-8 source (any `0xA0`-range byte, or a binary delta that is not valid UTF-8) aborts the process instead of a refusal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/handoff/send.py:58

chunk_findings.detail: The file forms reject anything that does not start with `diff --git`, but the `--commit` form returns `git show` stdout unchecked. An empty commit yields `show.ok` and `out == ""`, so `suggest` calls `events.propose` with an empty patch. A merge commit is shown without `-m`, so the payload is a combined diff (or empty), not a patch `git apply` can replay onto the owner tip. The same bytes supplied via `--blob` are refused.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/handoff/send.py:50

chunk_findings.detail: Refusals and the no-base notice do not name an exact next call. No live holder returns only `"{item} has no live lease holder to suggest to"` — no CLI or MCP follow-up. `SuggestError` strings for a missing `--reason` or a bad input likewise name no command. When `_owner_tip` is empty (`refs/heads/ddflow/{item}` missing and `item.base` empty), the owner line is `ddflow apply via patch-id (no base: blob-only suggestion)`, which is not a runnable command and omits reject, show, and expiry.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/handoff.py:44

chunk_findings.detail: `suggest` has no `evidence` argument and does not pass one into `events.propose`. `api.handoff.suggest` cannot forward it either. `--kind gate_fix --evidence CMD,EXIT` is dropped on this path, so a gate-fix suggestion is stored with no command/exit for the commit-time check the probe is supposed to fail open to.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/handoff/send.py:66

chunk_findings.detail: `_suggest` is the only declared CLI/MCP entry for `ddflow suggest`, and it never reads or forwards `--evidence`. The command contract is `ITEM (--commit|--diff|--blob) --reason [--kind gate_fix --evidence CMD,EXIT]`, but `Param`s and the `H.suggest(...)` call only pass item, reason, kind, commit, diff, blob, and agent. A caller that supplies evidence, e.g. `ddflow suggest ITEM --diff change.diff --reason "fix gate" --kind gate_fix --evidence "pytest,1"`, cannot record that probe result; the flag is not on the tool, so the suggestion is filed with no evidence (or the call is rejected as an unknown argument) and the commit-time check has nothing to fail open from.

data.decision: At bug found, a test file the bug's summary names (a path matching is_test_file) is auto-added to the fix task's globs, alongside the found/inherited scope, so the implementer can write the regression test as an edit to an existing tests/test_*.py without ddflow update --globs. This applies to ddflow-scoped bugs too, which otherwise inherit no files: a named test file is where the regression test goes, unlike a named source file, which is symptom-or-cause (Bc0b26248e3).
